title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS FIRST — (c) IS DUE TODAY, AND YESTERDAY'S REASON FOR CARRYING IT WAS WRONG BY FOUR DAYS: /skill-doctor shipped Sep 4 in v2.1.261, not Sep 8 in v2.1.266
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's own open decisions, plus one dated correction. The 14:00 fire on 09-09 wrote that the tool for the overdue-tomorrow action shipped yesterday, crediting v2.1.266 (Sep 8) with new skill diagnostics. Two independent dated sources put /skill-doctor in v2.1.261 on Sep 4 - it tracks whether each eligible skill was invoked and shows its context cost, alongside an Organization-policy line on /status and claude doctor, and bashOutputMaxChars/taskOutputMaxChars raising inline output to 128K characters. v2.1.266's 'policy and skill diagnostics' was a refinement of a command that already existed. One further gate no prior fire has named: /skill-doctor is a CLAUDE CODE command, run from the terminal where the session lives and unavailable over Remote Control - while the ~130-skill corpus loads into COWORK sessions, so running it means a Claude Code session on the Mac against the same plugin set, not a Cowork prompt. Standing list: (a) misalignment incident log - DUE TOMORROW, SEP 11, and bullet 2 changes what it should be. (b) Entra's four MCP controls as a config script - DUE SEP 12 (discover shadow servers, allow/block per tool, pin protocol version to 2026-07-28, pin transport). (c) /skill-doctor across the ~130-skill corpus - DUE TODAY, and runnable since Sep 4. (e) cadence-cost measurement before the Sep 14 Claude Code limit change - DUE SEP 12, two days out. (d) MCP Live! closed yesterday at 20:00 UTC unattended; it leaves the list.
bullets.how: YES, and the correction matters more than the calendar. Yesterday's fire built a rhetorical point out of 'the tool improved YESTERDAY while the deadline is TOMORROW,' and the tool had in fact been available for five days when that sentence was written. The lesson the 14:00 fire itself wrote - that a daily scan has no memory - cuts inward too: we misdated an item about our OWN toolchain, from a changelog we cite every day, because we read the newest entry rather than searching for the feature. Note the shape of every miss this week: Cognition ($2B, same-day, declared boundary), HiddenLayer ($100M, seven days, no backward sweep), and now /skill-doctor (four days, wrong version credited). Three mechanisms, one common property - WE CHECK WHAT IS NEWEST AND NEVER CHECK WHAT IS TRUE. On (c) there is no story left: the tool has existed six days, the deadline is today, and the only remaining unknown is a real one this fire surfaced - it may not be runnable from Cowork at all.

bullets.title: THE DAY'S LEAD — STANDING ACTION (a) SHIPPED AS A PRODUCT. Anthropic's Compliance API now returns consolidated server-hosted transcripts of Cowork AND Claude Code sessions, including TOOL-CALL CONTENT for web and MCP, skills and artifacts content, per-message IDs and timestamps
bullets.summary: Coverage extends across Cowork on desktop, web and mobile, and Claude Code in the CLI and desktop app. The session endpoints return one consolidated record per session rather than scattered logs: prompts and responses, TOOL CALLS CONTENT (web and MCP), skills and artifacts content captured as transcript text, and session metadata comprising verified user ID and email, organization ID, session and per-message IDs, and timestamps. It runs through the same Compliance API interface and existing Compliance Access Key already used for Claude chats - no separate integration. Bounds, stated because they decide applicability: it is CLAUDE ENTERPRISE ONLY, the local and remote session endpoints are stable for Cowork and Claude Code while Claude Science and Claude for Microsoft 365 coverage is in beta, and it explicitly EXCLUDES Claude Code on the web, Claude Code via the Claude Platform, and any session run on Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI or Microsoft Foundry.
bullets.how: YES, and it is the most consequential item this report has carried for our own exposure, for a reason no earlier fire could have predicted. Yesterday's Deadbugz bullet proved (a) was MIS-SPECIFIED: 'what did an agent touch that we did not authorise' cannot see a server whose ANSWERS change after vetting, and the log needed a second question - what changed in what a server told us, and when. Read the field list against that sentence: TOOL-CALL CONTENT FOR MCP, WITH PER-MESSAGE IDS AND TIMESTAMPS, IS PRECISELY THE SECOND QUESTION, ANSWERED BY CONSTRUCTION. We did not have to design the log; the shape arrived four days after we discovered we had specified it wrongly. The hard part is a plan gate, not a technical one: this is Enterprise-tier and nothing in our stack indicates we are on it, so the honest reading is not '(a) is solved' but '(a) is now a build-or-buy decision with a known spec instead of a blank page.' If Enterprise is reachable, (a) becomes procurement and the fastest close on this list. If not, we hand-roll it knowing the exact record to write - session ID, per-message ID, timestamp, the MCP tool called, and THE METADATA THAT SERVER RETURNED ON THAT CALL - which is a schema, not an aspiration. Note the quiet second-order fact: Anthropic capturing Cowork tool-call content server-side means our sessions already produce this record somewhere; the gap is our ACCESS to it, not its existence.

bullets.title: THE BUILT-IN BROWSER IS NOT AN ANNOUNCEMENT TO US — IT IS ALREADY IN THIS SESSION, AND IT COLLIDES WITH A LOCKED OPERATING RULE
bullets.summary: Cowork now runs its own browser inside the desktop app: when a task involves a website, a browser opens in a side panel and Claude opens sites, reads pages, clicks, types and fills forms in view, with the same browsing capabilities as Claude in Chrome but independent of whichever browser the user normally runs. It reached Pro, Max and Team on macOS, Windows and Linux with Enterprise admins able to enable it org-wide, and when the desktop app is online the built-in browser is also available in Cowork on web and mobile. The isolation property is load-bearing: Claude cannot see your tabs, bookmarks or saved passwords unless you explicitly import logins into it, SITE BY SITE.
bullets.how: YES, and uniquely among these items verification cost nothing: the mcp__Claude_Browser__* toolset is live in this very session alongside mcp__claude-in-chrome__*, so this is observed rather than reported. The collision is with two of our rules written when only one browser existed. Our locked rule is NEVER open a new Chrome window or tab - always attach to the already-open Chrome - and a family of skills (review-open-browser-tabs-first, chrome-automation-user-visibility, hermes-real-browser-only) exists because Bobby's PAID, LOGGED-IN subscriptions (Higgsfield, HBR, LinkedIn, GBP, SiteGround) live in that one profile. The built-in browser is a SECOND, EMPTY, CREDENTIAL-ISOLATED profile - both the opportunity and the trap. Opportunity: the consumer-LLM visibility scan (ChatGPT/Claude/Perplexity/Gemini for brand-insights/latest.json) is exactly the job that should NOT run in Bobby's authenticated Chrome, because his logged-in history is a confound in a brand-visibility measurement and driving his real tabs renders them blank to him - a documented, repeatedly-costly failure. A clean isolated profile is a BETTER INSTRUMENT for that scan. Trap: any credentialed job - GBP, SiteGround cache purge, Higgsfield, LinkedIn posting - will silently fail in the built-in browser because the logins are not there. So the rule needs a SPLIT, not a replacement: credentialed work stays in the attached Chrome; measurement work moves to the built-in browser. That is a one-line amendment to three skills and it removes a real confound from the only scan we run that produces a client-facing number.

bullets.title: AGENTS-RUN-GTM WAS PRICED AT $7.1B YESTERDAY, AND THE CUSTOMER LIST IS THE PART THAT SHOULD STING
bullets.summary: Clay closed a $115M Series D at a $7.1B valuation on Sep 9, led by Wellington with a16z, CapitalG, Meritech, Sequoia and StepStone participating - more than double the $3.1B it carried on its $100M Series C in August 2025. The product is AI software and agents that automate go-to-market: analysing company and customer data, recommending actions, and executing parts of the workflow. Customers passed 17,000, up from 10,000 a year earlier, and the named roster includes Anthropic, ElevenLabs, Google, OpenAI, Siemens and Stripe. Source-quality note: valuation and customer count are company-reported at announcement and unaudited, and the trade press repeats them; the round, the lead and the date are corroborated across BetaKit, SiliconANGLE and TechFundingNews.
bullets.how: MAYBE, and the honest tag is maybe rather than yes because nothing here is a tool we would adopt. What it is, is A PRICE ON OUR OWN THESIS, SET BY SOMEONE ELSE. PRAGMA sells the proposition that agents run the operating layer of a business and the operator is the product; Clay sells one slice - the GTM slice - and the market just paid $115M at 2.3x last year's valuation for it, with ANTHROPIC, GOOGLE AND OPENAI AS PAYING CUSTOMERS. Three readings that do not agree. Bullish: the category is real, funded and adopted at the top of the market, so the thesis is not the risk. Bearish: well-capitalised slice-takers are moving faster than the generalist, and 17,000 customers is a distribution moat no amount of answer-page craft closes. Actionable, and worth an hour: Clay's wedge was ONE WORKFLOW, EXECUTED TO A STANDARD, SOLD HORIZONTALLY - the opposite of our shape, which is many workflows for few clients. Keystone should read that comparison directly, because the question is not 'are we right' but 'are we shaped like the thing that gets funded.' Filed maybe because it changes no build this week; it changes what the operator pitch must answer when someone asks who else does this.

bullets.title: THE PAPER THAT NAMES THE THING /skill-doctor MEASURES — five context-quality criteria, and the two we systematically fail are ECONOMY and PROVENANCE
bullets.summary: 'Context Engineering: From Prompts to Corporate Multi-Agent Architecture' (arXiv 2603.09619) argues context engineering is a standalone discipline concerned with designing, structuring and managing the entire informational environment in which an agent decides, and proposes five quality criteria - relevance, sufficiency, isolation, economy, provenance - framing context as the agent's operating system. Adjacent work in the same line: 'Structured Context Engineering for File-Native Agentic Systems' (2602.05447), which finds architectural choices must be tailored to model capability, and 'Interpretable Context Methodology: Folder Structure as Agentic Architecture' (2603.16021). Source-quality note, stated plainly because the task asked for papers FROM THIS WEEK and these are not: 2603.09619 is a MARCH 2026 preprint, surfaced now, not new. It is carried under the same backfill rule that carried HiddenLayer yesterday, and the reason is in the applicability line. No prompt-engineering or agent-architecture paper published this week surfaced as significant on this pass.
bullets.how: YES, because it supplies vocabulary for a problem two other bullets describe without naming. ECONOMY is what /skill-doctor measures - every skill in the listing enters context on every turn whether invoked or not, which at ~130 skills is a standing tax we have never once quantified; standing action (c) is an economy audit and now has a word for what it audits. PROVENANCE is the criterion behind our own vironbox-provenance-gate - and bullet 2 is provenance arriving as INFRASTRUCTURE: a per-message record of which MCP server said what, when. ISOLATION is bullet 3's split-the-browsers argument in one word. The value is not novelty; it is that the five criteria give us a checklist to run the ~130-skill corpus against ONCE, and four of the five are already instrumented or shipping. Do not over-read a preprint: it is a framework paper, not a result, and it proves nothing. But when (c) runs today it should emit more than a prune list - it should emit an ECONOMY NUMBER we can put in front of (e)'s cadence-cost measurement on Sep 12, because those two are the same question asked from opposite ends.

praxis_lesson: Yesterday's three fires produced three correct rules - external clocks, boundary-is-not-coverage, memory - and zero completed actions, and the 14:00 fire said plainly that the rules were not the bottleneck. Today confirms that harder than intended, because THIS FIRE HAD TO RETRACT A CLAIM FROM YESTERDAY ABOUT OUR OWN TOOLCHAIN: /skill-doctor shipped Sep 4 in v2.1.261, not Sep 8 in v2.1.266, so the tool for the action due today has been available for six days and we built a rhetorical flourish on its being one day old. Line the week's three misses up - Cognition ($2B, same day, inside a declared boundary), HiddenLayer ($100M, seven days, no backward sweep), /skill-doctor (four days, wrong version credited from a changelog we cite daily) - and the common property is not boundary, not source count, and not memory. IT IS THAT WE CHECK WHAT IS NEWEST AND NEVER CHECK WHAT IS TRUE. A newest-first reader misdates its own tools; the correction is to search for the FEATURE and not read the top of the changelog, and it costs one query. Now the part that matters more than any method point. Standing action (a) has been named on six fires. Yesterday we learned from a live attacker that it was SPECIFIED WRONGLY - an authorised server's changing answers are invisible to a log that only asks what an agent touched. Today Anthropic shipped a product that returns MCP tool-call content with per-message IDs and timestamps, which is the corrected specification, four days later. THE WORLD HAS NOW SUPPLIED THE DEADLINE, THE ATTACKER, THE CAPITAL, THE VOCABULARY AND THE SCHEMA FOR THIS ONE ITEM, AND WE HAVE SUPPLIED NOTHING. So state the smallest true thing this report can still be judged on, without another rule attached: (c) is due today and has been runnable since Sep 4 - though this fire found a real gate, that it is a Claude Code command while the ~130-skill corpus loads into Cowork. (a) is due tomorrow and is no longer a design problem; it is one decision - Enterprise Compliance API, or hand-roll the five-field record bullet 2 spells out. Both are hours, not days. Six fires of diagnosis have produced a perfect specification of work that has not started, and the only honest measure of tomorrow's fire is whether it reports a number from /skill-doctor or a seventh reason.
